gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the two front-runners record almost the same total pixels per frame with all three channels on (Vantrue N4S 12.41 MP as 1944p + 1440p + 1440p, Redtiger F17 12.44 MP as labelled 4K + 1080p + 1080p), or that the N4S front is a 4:3 frame of 5.04 MP (61% of a 4K frame) and its cabin camera drops from 1944p to 1440p once the rear camera is connected.
standout_why: Compared against productbible.com (cited), dattatecblog.com (cited) and us.my-best.com (cited); vortexradar.com (cited) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Product Bible already gives the N4S's three-channel figures in prose ("1944p front, 1440p cabin and a 1440p rear camera rated IP67", STARVIS 2 in all three, $199.99), so the core row exists on a cited rival. It gives one figure per channel and has no per-mode table, no pixel counts, no 4:3 note, and it does not cover the Redtiger F17 or Rexing C3 at all. Dattatecblog gives the F17 only as "4K front + 1080P inside + 1080P rear" with "STARVIS 2 sensor" and no sensor model or megapixels. my-best lists neither the N4S nor the F17. No page puts the N4S and F17 on one pixel basis. The piece that would lift this to a 3, the base F17's front sensor model and megapixels, I could not source from an opened page.
decides: It confirms the Vantrue N4S for anyone who needs the cabin and rear views to be usable (rideshare, rear-end claims): each of those channels records 3.69 MP against the F17's labelled 2.07 MP, about 1.78 times the pixels, while the F17 puts its pixels in the front view. It also corrects ChatGPT's table, which set "Up to 3K" against "4K" as if they were the same kind of number: the N4S front is 2592 x 1944 in 4:3, and the "up to 2.5K" cabin figure of 1944p applies only in front + cabin mode, not with three channels. The N4S is $199.99 at vantrue.com today, inside the $200 line by one cent, is in an approved program (awin:vantrue) and has no record yet. The F17 stays the lower-priced alternative at $151.98 on Amazon. The finding does not settle whether the F17's front "4K" is a native 8 MP sensor.
